segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so I pulled up the pricing sheet before the call. For 68 seats on the standard plan, you're at $42 per user per month, billed annually, so the annual total comes to $34,272 before tax.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, that lines up with what I had. We may start with 62 seats on May 1 and add the last six after our June hiring class. Is that a problem contract-wise?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: No, that's fine. We can write the order form for 62 seats at go-live and include a provision that additional seats are added coterminous at the same rate. The billing tool will prorate those six if you add them in June.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. And for implementation, you had mentioned three weeks. We need the team trained before May 8. Is that still realistic?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, if we get signature by April 12, we can kick off April 15. That gives us data setup the first week, admin training April 24, and end-user sessions on May 2 and May 3.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. Our finance team also asked if the invoice can reference PO 44718 and break out subscription separate from onboarding.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. Onboarding is the one-time $4,500 line item, and subscription is separate. I'll put PO 44718 on the order form and make sure it carries through to the invoice.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Term is 12 months, right? We are not ready for a multi-year this round.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct, 12 months. Renewal date would be April 30, 2027 if we start May 1, 2026. Standard renewal notice is 30 days before the end of term.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Send the updated order form today and I can route it for signature. Legal already reviewed the terms, so it should be pretty quick.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I'll send it by 2 pm central with the seat count at 62, the same $42 rate, onboarding split out, and the PO included.
